label: AQ 0031
title: The cache that ate the batch

questions.q: Does prefix caching make tokens stream faster?
questions.a: No. It skips prefill work (the pass over the prompt), so the first token comes sooner. Later decode steps still read the whole cache.
Quality can drop. And split across 8 GPUs, one KV head can't be divided: the Llama 2 paper says you copy the cache to every GPU or split by batch.

teach.title: How it works: the bill, then the levers

questions.q: What happens when the cache fills mid-answer?
questions.a: vLLM pauses the newest requests. It moves their blocks to CPU memory, or drops them and rebuilds them later.

teach.title: How it works: the bill, then the levers

questions.q: Why are keys and values cached but not queries?
questions.a: A token's query only matters while that token is being made. Its key and value are read by every later token.

questions.q: Llama 3.1 8B, 2-byte cache: how much does a 16k-token request take?
questions.a: 128 KiB × 16,384 = 2 GiB. Half the 32k figure, because the cache grows with length.

teach.title: How it works: the bill, then the levers

questions.q: Why don't more FLOPs fix slow long-context decode?
questions.a: Each step waits on loading the weights and the whole cache.
